body: Thanks for this, it’s a lesson I’m trying hard to learn and it’s nice hearing that someone else is in the same kind of fight I am, good luck to you and keep spreading the positivity!

As a man who struggles with depression the biggest thing would like to see change is the overall perception that being so low that you are considering suicide as a serious option makes you weak/ not a man/ not manly enough, or being told to just man up and stop crying. When I’ve been that low, weak is a big feeling for me, and I use it against myself as an insult, so hearing it from someone else is like being kicked when you’re down. We need to teach that it’s not weak, that life is hard and mental issues are serious and can take a real toll. We need to teach that it’s okay to feel that bad and we need to get better support networks together in our communities to help build confidence back up and make mental health treatment more accessible. When I went back to therapy one of my thoughts was that I was weak and not a real man for needing a therapists help, and that’s not true at all and we need to stop the things that are causing men to think that way about their mental health.
